newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's ruling centre-right seen winning poll.
newsitem.headline: France's ruling centre-right seen winning poll.

text.p: France's ruling centre-right will retain a large majority in a snap parliamentary election, according to the first opinion poll carried out since President Jacques Chirac announced the election for May 25-June 1.
The CSA poll released on Tuesday said the ruling coalition would win 332 seats to 221 for the left.
The survey said the Socialists would win 201 of the National Assembly's 577 seats, with the Communists winning 20.
The Greens and the far-right National Front would win one seat each.
The poll of 1,002 adults to be published on Wednesday in the daily Le Parisien was carried out on Tuesday and was the first survey released since Chirac's announcement on Monday.
The centre-right coalition of Prime Minister Alain Juppe held 80 percent of the seats in the assembly dissolved by Chirac.
